{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVMWpgs8AAAABZlIhjg", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4BnW-xzhDLq7k", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4BnW-x", "number": 75, "title": "Add external FM-PAC on MSX1/MSX2 with independent cartridge mapping and SRAM", "body": "## Problem

At baseline `fb5e220db81a609fb8bbe0eab1cdd7696f589b9e`, FM installation accepts only the MSX2 internal-style profile. `crates/msx-core/src/lib.rs` gates its ports and synthesis by model; external FM-PAC memory registers, banked firmware and battery-backed SRAM are absent. Existing cartridge/accessory installation also shares slot 1.

Software therefore cannot discover or program a conventional external FM-PAC on MSX1/MSX2, or use its saves alongside a game cartridge. Commercial benefit is inferred from the hardware interface and documented accessory use; no commercial failure or successful gameplay was observed.

## Expected outcome

Provide one explicitly optional original FM-PAC profile, reusing the existing YM2413 synthesis. Support independently supplied 64 KiB firmware, memory/I/O controls, four ROM banks and retained SRAM through core, Wasm and browser. Keep the game cartridge or SCC-I and disk interface independently installed.

Use an optional expansion of primary slot 2 on both models: disk remains in 2-0, FM-PAC occupies 2-1/page 1. Without FM-PAC, preserve the existing slot topology. This is a selected virtual configuration, not a claim about a complete historical machine.

## Context

Clean local HEAD matches inspected GitHub main. The open Issue/PR collection is empty. [Issue #65](https://github.com/takahirox/msx-rust/issues/65) explicitly deferred external FM-PAC and MSX1 FM support.

References inspected:

- [MSX-MUSIC hardware chapter](https://map.grauw.nl/resources/datapack/Vol2-3.1MSX-MUSICHardware.pdf), sections 3.1.2–3.1.4: external memory access, identification, reset-disabled I/O, enable interaction and programming delays.
- [Pinned openMSX MSXFmPac.cc](https://github.com/openMSX/openMSX/blob/26e1e4945df406e250a05122889f88d40edd828b/src/sound/MSXFmPac.cc): original-profile banking, SRAM and register decoding. Its memory access remains independent of the I/O enable latch. This is behavioral corroboration, not new physical validation.
- [PAC SRAM investigation](https://gigamix.hatenablog.com/entry/devmsx/pac-sram-access) and [upstream save guidance](https://github.com/openMSX/openMSX/blob/26e1e4945df406e250a05122889f88d40edd828b/doc/manual/faq.html): usable SRAM excludes the two unlock locations; accessory storage is shared across games.

Relevant paths include core bus/reset/mixer and firmware fixtures, Wasm uploads/save access, `web/app.js`, `web/saves.js`, native FM/slot/SRAM tests and browser lifecycle tests. Current [CI logs](https://github.com/takahirox/msx-rust/actions/runs/40080797098/job/120833753209) report 312 Rust and 206 browser passes, including internal FM and Philips/SCC-I coexistence. Those tests do not establish external FM-PAC behavior. Planning ran no builds or tests.

Exact analog output, fast-write silicon behavior, vendor FM-BIOS execution and commercial compatibility remain unestablished. Retain the existing synthesis/timing limitations. MSX-AUDIO, standalone PAC variants and generalized cartridge expansion remain separate work.

## Pre-merge acceptance

- [ ] Implement the stated slot placement and per-page secondary selection, including inverted FFFFh readback and latch precedence whenever expanded primary slot 2 occupies page 3. Reset its selectors to zero. Preserve MSX2 slot-3 expansion and MSX1 fixed RAM. Test hidden-slot isolation, page boundaries and disk register separation; removal restores the previous topology.
- [ ] Map the exact supplied firmware bytes read-only at 4000h–7FFFh through four 16 KiB banks. Implement 7FF7h low-two-bit bank selection; 7FF6h retains bits 0/4. Implement 5FFEh=4Dh and 5FFFh=69h unlock, 4000h–5FFDh SRAM, unlock readback, protected writes and upper-window FFh reads except control registers. Bit 4 clears/prevents unlocking. Reset restores bank/control/unlock state while retaining SRAM; initialize new SRAM explicitly. Cover partial unlocks, relocking, ignored bits and reads beneath overlays.
- [ ] Route 7FF4h/7FF5h memory writes independently of I/O enable. Bit 0 gates external 7Ch/7Dh writes only, using existing low-byte port decoding. Port reads remain FFh. Hiding firmware or clearing I/O enable must preserve already programmed sound and phase. Keep internal MSX-MUSIC behavior intact; when both devices are installed, maintain independent chips and broadcast I/O to each enabled recipient. Do not add host-side discovery, automatic enable or duplicate-sound suppression.
- [ ] Add transactional explicit core/Wasm/browser installation and removal, validating the 64 KiB profile before commit. Preserve selected system firmware, game cartridge/SRAM or SCC-I, disk interface/media/changes and cassette position. Retain FM-PAC installation/SRAM across reset, firmware, cartridge and model transitions; reset chip/control state consistently. Failed, canceled, stale or allocation-failed imports preserve the running session. Do not patch firmware or synthesize production identification strings.
- [ ] Provide independent FM-PAC SRAM persistence and backup/restore using the existing safeguards. Use a separate accessory profile/firmware identity, independent of the active game, and document shared storage. Validate the exact 8190-byte payload, version, identity and checksum atomically without weakening existing cartridge-save validation. Preserve cross-tab conflict, storage-error and recovery/export behavior; never persist firmware bytes.
- [ ] Add independently authored native register/slot sequences and executable redistributable Z80 firmware/cartridge diagnostics for both models. Demonstrate discovery, banked execution, memory programming while I/O-disabled, enabled/disabled port writes, exact save round trips and hidden-device audio. Record representative assertion failures against the baseline and corrected results. Use literal expected bytes and independent PCM/pitch expectations; nonzero audio alone is insufficient.
- [ ] Exercise compiled Wasm/browser imports and scheduled PCM at `/` and `/msx-rust/`, including save recovery after reload, game replacement, reset/removal, mute/resume, pause and import failures. Include combined game or SCC-I, Philips disk transfers, PSG and FM-PAC with exact memory/disk results. Preserve sample counts, partition invariance, bounded mixing and unchanged existing PCM when FM-PAC is absent. Respect documented write spacing in valid diagnostics.
- [ ] Preserve existing MSX1/MSX2, video, input, audio, disk, SRAM, firmware, Wasm/browser and ownership/provenance behavior where affected. Keep the core dependency-free. Independently author device decoding from behavioral references; retain existing synthesis notices. Update profile, save, compatibility and distribution documentation without claiming vendor firmware or commercial playability.
- [ ] Before merge, the Coordinator runs and reports README checks: `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo test --workspace --locked`, `./scripts/build.sh`, `node scripts/check-dist.mjs`, `npm test`, and `git diff --check`, with documented dependency setup as needed. Complete source-Issue/full-diff review and resolve blocking findings. Distinguish passed, failed, skipped and unperformed checks. Proprietary firmware, human gameplay and physical hardware are not prerequisites.

## Optional validation

Before merge, compare original diagnostic traces with a pinned reference implementation or available physical FM-PAC evidence. Exercise already lawfully available firmware/software, documenting slot-scanning limitations and exact observations. These comparisons were not performed during planning and are not mandatory.

## Required post-merge verification

None.
